text.tspan: Page 4, About this release candidate
What the pen says, word for word, and what it means
THE MAKING-OF OUT OF THE READER'S WAY
“the ZX FOUNDER doesn't care yet → maybe at
the end of the Book”
The reader does not care how the book was made, not yet:
About this release candidate moves to the end.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“is this a better name than ZX developer?”
A naming question: is 'ZX founder' a better name for the
reader than 'ZX developer'? (Asked again on page 8.)
THE MAKING-OF OUT OF THE READER'S WAY
“logistics”
How the chapters say where their sources ran out is
logistics, not reading.
THE MAKING-OF OUT OF THE READER'S WAY
“this is the story & workflow detail ↓ then
they should not be here”
The story of rc1 and the workflow do not belong on page 4.
A RELEASE, NOT A DRAFT
“remove”
Remove the paragraph about placeholder chapters from the
reader's book.
A RELEASE, NOT A DRAFT
“WRONG [over: not a version]”
'This is a candidate, not a version' is wrong: this is a
release.
A RELEASE, NOT A DRAFT
“this is an RC which will be added to
Leanpub & sold ✓ ... i.e. we are selling &
shipping this book now”
The release candidate goes on Leanpub and is sold, now.
A RELEASE, NOT A DRAFT
“this RCx → RELEASE CANDIDATE ↓ i.e. this
should be a release → not a draft”
Spell out 'release candidate', and treat it as a release,
not a draft.
